basic_info.title: Scaling Laws for Single-Agent Reinforcement Learning

method.notes: Mean episode return does not vary smoothly with scale, so introduces INTRINSIC PERFORMANCE (minimum compute to reach a given return across a model family), which scales as a power law in model size and environment interactions on Procgen, 1v1 Dota 2, and MNIST-horizon toys. Optimal model size scales as a power law in compute budget, and optimal RL model sizes are SMALLER than supervised intuition suggests at a given compute level — relevant caution against reflexively scaling the P2 world model.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Not a map-matching or world-model paper; methodology reference for RL model sizing.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Cited for the smaller-than-expected optimal RL model size and the intrinsic-performance construction.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Indirect: sizing guidance for any future P2/actor scale-up.

uncertain: Environments are on-policy game/procgen domains; transfer of coefficients to imagination-trained world-model RL over road graphs unverified.
